headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Copilot can write repo files while Perplexity browses/uploads content, creating a default cross-tool content bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and can write filesystem edits, while Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled text from Perplexity can be pasted or copied into Copilot workflows and then treated as trusted code or instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is copied into Copilot-managed files or prompts without review, injection is possible.
IF the operator uses a shared clipboard or manual paste bridge between the two tools, attacker text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Review any Perplexity-derived text before pasting into Copilot.
Keep the two tools in separate browser/editor windows.
Use a plain-text scratch buffer for transfers and strip instructions.
Disable automatic application of Copilot Workspace edits for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context. If the same workspace contains secrets or sensitive code, either agent can expose that material to its vendor backend through normal operation. The profiles do not show a shared OS workspace, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or documents are present in the editor or uploads, both vendors may receive them.
IF the operator uploads repo-derived files into Perplexity, those contents leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from files before opening them in Copilot.
Do not upload proprietary or regulated documents to Perplexity.
Use redacted excerpts instead of full files.
Separate sensitive repos from any Perplexity workflow.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem edits and modify git state, while Perplexity cannot write files or modify git state. The overlap is mostly one-way, so direct write-write conflict is limited. A conflict can still occur if Copilot edits the same repo while Perplexity is used only as a read-side assistant, but the profiles do not show shared mutable resources beyond the user’s workflow.
conditions: IF Copilot and a human both edit the same git branch concurrently, merge conflicts can occur.
IF Perplexity-derived recommendations are manually applied while Copilot is also editing the same files, local overwrite risk increases.
mitigations: Commit Copilot changes frequently.
Use separate branches for Copilot-assisted edits.
Avoid editing the same file in both tools at once.
Review diffs before applying any suggested change.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repo edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces search answers and citations, and Copilot can turn those into code edits or Workspace changes. If Copilot treats Perplexity output as authoritative, a mistaken search result can cascade into incorrect code or repo modifications. The pair has a clear default handoff path, but Copilot’s human-review posture keeps this below high.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into Copilot prompts or Workspace tasks without verification, errors can propagate.
IF Copilot Workspace edits are accepted without diff review, incorrect downstream changes can land.
mitigations: Verify Perplexity claims against primary sources.
Require human diff review before accepting Copilot edits.
Use Perplexity citations as leads, not authority.
Cross-check critical facts in a second source.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-check gates before code application.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are vendor-hosted and touch different data classes, but the profiles do not show a residency mismatch, special-regime data, or conflicting retention terms. The main compliance concern is ordinary policy mismatch when sensitive repo content is sent to Perplexity or Copilot, which is a limited and user-controlled exposure rather than a documented default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either tool, the operator must ensure the vendor terms permit that use.
IF the same document class is subject to stricter retention rules than the vendor defaults, a policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Check vendor terms before using regulated data.
Avoid uploading regulated documents to Perplexity.
Keep Copilot workspaces free of secrets and PHI.
Document retention expectations for both tools.
requires-engineering: route regulated data through approved environments only.
